We use a single file from the **World Happiness Report 2025**: `WHR25_Data_Figure_2.1v3.xlsx`, the data behind the report's headline Figure 2.1. Unlike the older year-by-year CSV releases, this is one already-harmonised table, so the columns are identical across every year and no cross-year schema-fixing is needed.

## Shape of the data

Each row represents **one country in one report year**, so the pair **`(country, year)`** uniquely identifies an observation.

|  |  |
|----|----|
| **Rows** | 1,969 country-year observations |
| **Columns** | 13 |
| **Years** | 2011–2024 (2013 is absent from the file) |
| **Countries** | 168 distinct countries overall, with roughly 140–160 reported in any given year |
| **Unit / row identity** | one country in one year → `(country, year)` |

Row counts vary a little from year to year (from ~137 in 2022 to ~158 in 2014) because the set of surveyed countries changes slightly each year.

## Columns

| Column (as in the file) | What it is |
|----|----|
| `Year` | Report year (part of the row identity) |
| `Rank` | Position in that year's global ranking |
| `Country name` | The nation — part of the row identity |
| `Life evaluation (3-year average)` ★ | Cantril-ladder life evaluation, 0–10 — the **target variable** |
| `Lower whisker` / `Upper whisker` | Confidence bounds around the life-evaluation estimate |
| `Explained by: Log GDP per capita` | Estimated contribution of income to the score |
| `Explained by: Social support` | Contribution of having someone to count on |
| `Explained by: Healthy life expectancy` | Contribution of healthy longevity |
| `Explained by: Freedom to make life choices` | Contribution of freedom over life choices |
| `Explained by: Generosity` | Contribution of charitable behaviour |
| `Explained by: Perceptions of corruption` | Contribution of perceived honesty / low corruption |
| `Dystopia + residual` | Baseline plus the unexplained remainder |

★ = target variable.

## A subtlety that shapes the whole analysis

**The six "Explained by" columns are not raw measurements.**

**What they actually are:** each `Explained by:` column is the estimated *contribution* of that factor to the country's score — not the raw value (e.g. it is not GDP in dollars, but how much income is estimated to lift that country's ladder score).

**They are additive:** the six contributions plus `Dystopia + residual` sum — up to rounding — exactly to the life-evaluation score. We checked this on the file itself: the largest gap between the reported score and the summed parts is about **0.003**. The bars in the report literally stack to the total.

**Why it matters:** a model that "predicts" the score from these six columns will fit near-perfectly almost by construction. We keep this in mind when reading the regression in Q2 — a high R² is partly built into how the columns are defined.

## Missing values

The factor columns are not populated for every country-year, especially generosity and perceptions of corruption in the earlier years. Keeping only complete cases (no missing value across the score and all six factors) drops the data from 1,969 to **868 rows** and, as a side effect, narrows the usable range to **2019–2024**. The full breakdown is documented in the [Initial data analysis](project_proposal.qmd#initial-data-analysis) section on the home page.

## Source & Licence

**Dataset:** World Happiness Report 2025 — *Data for Figure 2.1*

**Published by:** the World Happiness Report ([worldhappiness.report](https://worldhappiness.report)), produced by the Wellbeing Research Centre at the University of Oxford together with Gallup and the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network.

**Underlying source:** Gallup World Poll — the Cantril-ladder life-evaluation question.

**Coverage:** one harmonised file, report years 2011–2024.

**Attribution:** the data is published for public and research use on the World Happiness Report website. As good academic practice we credit it as: "World Happiness Report 2025, *Data for Figure 2.1*. Underlying data: Gallup World Poll."
